concepts.name: Metacognition
concepts.short_description: Thinking about thinking; confidence calibration, error monitoring, strategy selection.

concepts.name: Nash Equilibrium
concepts.short_description: Stable strategy profiles where no agent benefits from unilateral deviation; mixed strategies, coordination games.

concepts.name: Pragmatics
concepts.short_description: Context-dependent meaning beyond literal semantics; implicature, speech acts, Grice's maxims.

defining_structures: a first-order process (decide/answer) and a second-order process that reads a signal about it
a confidence variable attached to each first-order output
a control arm: monitoring output changes strategy (stop, retry, ask, abstain)
invariants: calibration: among outputs tagged with confidence p, a fraction p is correct
resolution: confidence ranks correct above incorrect outputs
transformations: strategy switch triggered by low confidence
conserved_quantities: none strictly; the ranking of items by confidence is preserved under monotone recalibration
failure_modes: monitor sharing the first-order error (correlated blind spot)
dynamics: confidence accumulates with evidence over time
learning of the confidence map from feedback
locality: monitor has access only to internal signals, not ground truth
local to one agent's own process
memory: track record of past accuracy by context
identity: the self whose accuracy is being modelled; the monitor must know which process it watches
reproduction: copying a calibrated confidence map to another agent does not transfer if first-order skill differs
selection: selection of strategies/tasks by expected accuracy
information: mutual information between confidence and correctness
metacognitive efficiency: resolution relative to first-order sensitivity
constraint: the monitor cannot be more informative than the signals it reads

defining_structures: a profile where each strategy is a best response to the others
invariants: existence of at least one mixed equilibrium in finite games
indifference among supported pure strategies in a mixed equilibrium
transformations: adding a constant or positive affine transform to a player's payoffs leaves equilibria unchanged
conserved_quantities: equilibrium set under positive affine payoff transforms
in zero-sum games, the game value
dynamics: replicator dynamics; equilibria as rest points
locality: deviations are unilateral: stability checked one player at a time
each player sees only own payoff
memory: history in repeated games enables reputation
fictitious play memory of opponent frequencies
reproduction: in evolutionary reading, strategies reproduce by payoff
selection: equilibrium selection: salience, risk dominance, payoff dominance
information: private types and beliefs in Bayesian games
common knowledge of rationality as an assumption
constraint: mutual consistency: every strategy constrained by all others

defining_structures: cooperative maxims: quantity, quality, relation, manner
invariants: listener assumes cooperativity unless evidence against
scalar alternatives: saying the weaker form implicates the stronger is not true
transformations: flouting a maxim to trigger reinterpretation
accommodation of presupposition into common ground
conserved_quantities: common ground grows monotonically within a cooperative exchange except under explicit repair
failure_modes: over-enrichment (reading implicature that was not meant)
dynamics: conventionalization of implicatures over repeated use
locality: meaning depends on local context and the alternatives the speaker could have said
identity: speaker intent; who is committed to what
reproduction: conventions spread by imitation across speakers
selection: speaker selects among alternative utterances by informativeness and cost
information: meaning carried by choice among alternatives, not only by form

unexplained: whether confidence reports can hold stable meaning when speakers have incentives
whether metacognitive precision limits which pragmatic equilibria are reachable
whether any interpretation needs all three concepts rather than two
which mechanisms reduce to two-concept stories (knockouts marked weak)
whether metacognitive noise acts as a continuous control on equilibrium informativeness or as a threshold
how to separate emergent hedge meaning from trivially shaped payoffs
whether L4 (private/public calibration gap) and L1 (hedge reliability) disagree in any regime
whether deviation-regret (L3) is small because of true equilibrium or because learning stalled
all worlds are specified, none run
whether the interaction effect in W1 survives a payoff family other than the one chosen
whether results are properties of best-response dynamics rather than of equilibria

hypotheses.statement: Confidence reports are speech acts inside a game: hedges ('certain', 'probably') acquire meaning only as an equilibrium between speakers and listeners, and the informativeness of that equilibrium is bounded by the speaker's metacognitive resolution. Experiment: vary metacognitive noise and measure the information carried by emergent hedges.

Implicature is a fixed point of recursive modelling (speaker models listener models speaker); metacognition is the controller that decides how deep to recurse on each utterance. Experiment: compare fixed-depth against self-monitored adaptive-depth interpretation on accuracy per unit reasoning.

Metacognition is itself an internal game: a generator and a monitor inside one agent reach a Nash equilibrium over output/withhold, and their internal messages are context-dependent (pragmatic) rather than literal. Experiment: split an agent into two payoff-bearing modules and test whether calibrated abstention is an equilibrium of the internal game.

Monitoring one's own interpretive uncertainty ('did I understand?') sets the rate of clarification requests, and the speaker's redundancy and the listener's clarification threshold settle into an equilibrium set by the cost ratio. Experiment: sweep clarification cost and locate the equilibrium threshold.

Equilibrium selection in coordination games is done by pragmatic salience, and metacognition estimates whether the partner shares the salience (shared context). Experiment: coordination with partially shared context and confidence-gated fallback to explicit signalling.

Strategic miscalibration: when listeners weight messages by stated confidence, stated confidence inflates and listeners pragmatically discount it; the resulting equilibrium separates a private (internal) calibration from a public (conventional) one. Experiment: measure the private-public calibration gap under different listener payoff rules.

Maxim flouting is only interpretable by a listener who monitors its own expectation of informativeness: a metacognitive surprise signal about the utterance (not about the world) triggers reinterpretation, and the speaker's flouting strategy is in equilibrium with that detector. Experiment: vary the listener's surprise-detector precision and measure non-literal interpretation success.

Hedge-token equilibrium: speakers attach one of K meaningless tokens to each answer; listeners choose accept or verify-at-cost. Under best-response dynamics tokens become calibrated confidence labels, and the mutual information between token and correctness is capped by the speaker's metacognitive resolution and collapses when speaker-listener interests diverge.

concept_contributions.Metacognition: the private confidence signal that the speaker can condition tokens on; its noise sets an upper bound on token informativeness
concept_contributions.Nash Equilibrium: stability of the token-to-confidence map; babbling vs informative equilibria; collapse under interest conflict
concept_contributions.Pragmatics: tokens have no literal meaning; meaning is the listener's inference from which token was chosen among alternatives

knockouts.Metacognition: tokens cannot correlate with correctness; only the babbling equilibrium remains
knockouts.Nash Equilibrium: without mutual best response, token meanings are arbitrary and drift
knockouts.Pragmatics: with fixed literal numeric confidence the question becomes pure calibration; no emergent convention to study

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: a plain sender-receiver signalling game whose state is the speaker's confidence bin; metacognitive noise is just state noise

questions.what_exists: speakers with answer+confidence, listeners with accept/verify, K tokens
questions.what_changes: speaker token policy, listener response policy
questions.what_persists: the token-to-confidence mapping once at equilibrium
questions.what_can_reproduce: token conventions via imitation in the population
questions.what_can_transfer: a converged token convention to a new task with a different accuracy distribution
questions.distinguishing_observable: MI(token; correctness) as a function of metacognitive noise and interest conflict jointly; the simpler alternative predicts a separable effect, the mechanism predicts an interaction (conflict threshold shifts with noise)

hypotheses.statement: Metacognitively gated recursion depth: a listener interprets utterances by level-k reasoning over alternatives and stops recursing when its self-estimated interpretive uncertainty falls below a threshold; the threshold is in equilibrium with how deeply speakers design their utterances.

concept_contributions.Metacognition: the stopping rule: uncertainty about one's own interpretation
concept_contributions.Nash Equilibrium: speaker's design depth and listener's reading depth are mutual best responses under effort cost
concept_contributions.Pragmatics: the recursion is over alternative utterances (scalar implicature)

knockouts.Metacognition: fixed depth; accuracy same on easy items, wasted effort on easy and errors on hard
knockouts.Nash Equilibrium: depth tuned by listener alone; speaker depth fixed; no co-adaptation
knockouts.Pragmatics: recursion over world states only; reduces to generic anytime inference

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: fixed level-2 reasoning, which may already capture most implicatures

questions.what_exists: referential contexts, utterances with literal extensions, depth-limited reasoners
questions.what_can_transfer: thresholds to contexts with different ambiguity rates
questions.distinguishing_observable: depth spent per item correlates with item ambiguity (Spearman) and adaptive depth matches fixed-depth accuracy with fewer steps

hypotheses.statement: Clarification equilibrium: the listener asks for clarification when its posterior over referents has max below tau; the speaker chooses redundancy r. The pair (tau*, r*) is an interior Nash equilibrium whose location moves predictably with the cost of asking and the cost of words.

concept_contributions.Metacognition: posterior-max as the listener's monitored interpretive confidence
concept_contributions.Nash Equilibrium: joint stability of tau and r
concept_contributions.Pragmatics: redundancy and clarification are speech-act choices that depend on shared context

knockouts.Metacognition: listener cannot tell when it misunderstood; clarification becomes random and wasteful
knockouts.Nash Equilibrium: optimize tau alone for fixed r: a decision problem, no trade-off between parties
knockouts.Pragmatics: weak: a generic noisy channel with retransmission (ARQ) gives the same structure

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: automatic repeat request with a fixed error-detection threshold in a noisy channel

questions.what_exists: objects with features, speakers, listeners, clarify action
questions.what_is_selected: tau and r by expected payoff
questions.what_can_transfer: tau* to new object sets with the same ambiguity rate
questions.distinguishing_observable: communicative success at equilibrium drops when listener confidence is replaced by a random score with the same marginal

hypotheses.statement: Utterance-surprise gate: the listener keeps a model of how informative a cooperative speaker should be in this context; an utterance that under-informs relative to that model triggers non-literal reinterpretation. Speakers flout only when the listener's gate is precise enough for flouting to pay.

concept_contributions.Metacognition: surprise about the utterance relative to self-predicted informativeness
concept_contributions.Nash Equilibrium: flouting rate and gate precision co-stabilize
concept_contributions.Pragmatics: maxim of quantity and its flouting

knockouts.Metacognition: no gate; flouting is always read literally and dies out
knockouts.Pragmatics: surprise-triggered re-analysis without the notion of cooperative informativeness: generic anomaly detection

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: a listener with a larger literal lexicon that simply includes the flouted form's secondary meaning

questions.what_is_selected: flouting when it saves cost and is understood
questions.distinguishing_observable: equilibrium flouting rate is a step function of gate precision

hypotheses.statement: Internal parliament: a generator and a monitor inside one agent have separate payoffs (generator rewarded for answering, monitor for avoiding errors); calibrated abstention is a Nash equilibrium of this internal game and the monitor's messages to the generator take meaning from task context.

concept_contributions.Nash Equilibrium: abstention policy as mutual best response between modules
concept_contributions.Pragmatics: monitor signals interpreted relative to task context

knockouts.Nash Equilibrium: a single joint objective gives the same abstention policy directly
knockouts.Pragmatics: weak: internal signals could be literal scalars with no loss; pragmatic contribution is thin

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: a single agent maximizing accuracy minus abstention cost with a confidence threshold

questions.distinguishing_observable: abstention threshold differs from the joint-objective optimum only when payoffs are misaligned; otherwise indistinguishable

hypotheses.statement: Confidence inflation with pragmatic discounting: when listeners weight speakers by stated confidence, speakers inflate; listeners learn to discount; the equilibrium has public confidence words whose meaning is shifted from private calibrated confidence, producing a measurable private-public calibration gap that vanishes under proper-scoring listeners.

concept_contributions.Metacognition: private calibrated confidence that exists separately from what is said
concept_contributions.Nash Equilibrium: inflation and discount as mutual best responses
concept_contributions.Pragmatics: public words mean 'discounted' values by convention, not by literal content

knockouts.Nash Equilibrium: without the listener's counter-adaptation, inflation runs to saturation with no stable shifted convention
knockouts.Pragmatics: numeric reports with a literal reading: inflation becomes lying, not convention shift

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: a cheap-talk game with a speaker bias parameter; the 'gap' is just the bias

questions.what_exists: speakers with private confidence, listeners with weighting rules, a word scale
questions.what_changes: speaker word map, listener decoding map
questions.what_can_transfer: a discounted convention to a population of honest speakers (predicted to under-trust them)
questions.distinguishing_observable: gap between private ECE and public-literal ECE while listener-decoded ECE stays low

hypotheses.statement: Content-confidence channel split: a channel of fixed capacity must carry both the answer and its confidence; at equilibrium confidence moves out of the explicit channel into implicature (e.g. choice of phrasing) when context makes it recoverable.

concept_contributions.Nash Equilibrium: allocation of bits stable against deviations
concept_contributions.Pragmatics: implicit transmission through choice among alternatives

knockouts.Metacognition: only content to send; no split
knockouts.Nash Equilibrium: weak: a single designer optimizing the code gives the same allocation

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: joint source coding by a single optimizer

questions.what_can_transfer: codes to contexts with less shared ground (predicted failure)
questions.distinguishing_observable: fraction of confidence information carried implicitly as a function of shared context

hypotheses.statement: Self-as-model substitution: agents approximate the partner's strategy by their own self-model (metacognitive access used as a proxy for common knowledge); equilibria reached this way are correct in homogeneous populations and systematically miscoordinate in heterogeneous ones, with miscoordination concentrated on context-dependent (pragmatic) signals.

concept_contributions.Nash Equilibrium: fixed points of projected best responses
concept_contributions.Pragmatics: context-dependent signals are where projection errors bite

knockouts.Metacognition: must learn partner model from data; slower but unbiased
knockouts.Nash Equilibrium: no fixed point concept; just projection bias
knockouts.Pragmatics: literal signals are robust to projection; the effect vanishes

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: false-consensus bias in a coordination game

questions.what_exists: agents of two types, coordination tasks with literal and context-dependent signals
questions.distinguishing_observable: miscoordination rate difference between context-dependent and literal signals in mixed-type pairs

hypotheses.statement: Common-ground ledger with uncertainty: each agent keeps a ledger of established facts plus a metacognitive estimate of whether each entry is shared; acknowledgement acts are spent on entries with low shared-estimate; equilibrium acknowledgement rate depends on channel loss.

concept_contributions.Metacognition: estimate that one's own ledger entry is shared
concept_contributions.Nash Equilibrium: acknowledgement rates as mutual best responses

knockouts.Nash Equilibrium: weak: a fixed protocol from a designer works equally well

questions.distinguishing_observable: ack allocation concentrates on uncertain entries vs uniform

hypotheses.statement: Mixed-strategy ambiguity cycles: speakers randomize between explicit and ambiguous forms; listeners' interpretive vigilance tracks the recent ambiguity rate; the population cycles around a mixed equilibrium, and listeners with better metacognitive tracking damp the cycles.

concept_contributions.Metacognition: tracking one's own recent misunderstanding rate to set vigilance
concept_contributions.Nash Equilibrium: mixed equilibrium as the centre of cycles
concept_contributions.Pragmatics: ambiguity as a cheap but risky form

knockouts.Metacognition: vigilance tracks nothing; cycle amplitude grows or is set by learning rate only
knockouts.Pragmatics: any two-action cost/risk trade-off would cycle the same way

questions.what_exists: speakers with a mix, listeners with vigilance
questions.distinguishing_observable: cycle amplitude vs listener tracking precision

hypotheses.statement: Reliability-tagged lexicon mutation: each word carries a metacognitive reliability tag; mutations that reassign a word's meaning are accepted only if the resulting lexicon remains a Nash equilibrium of the referential game; low-reliability words mutate more.

concept_contributions.Metacognition: per-word reliability estimate steering mutation rate

knockouts.Metacognition: uniform mutation; slower convergence but same end states
knockouts.Pragmatics: weak: any code optimisation with adaptive mutation

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: adaptive mutation rate proportional to local error

questions.distinguishing_observable: time to equilibrium lexicon vs uniform mutation

hypotheses.statement: Hedges acquire meaning only after self-calibration: in a developing agent, confidence tokens stay babbling until its internal confidence map reaches a resolution threshold, then snap to an informative equilibrium; the order (calibrate first, then hedge) is required, and reversing it locks in a babbling convention.

concept_contributions.Nash Equilibrium: babbling equilibrium as an absorbing state

knockouts.Metacognition: no development; either always babbling or always informative
knockouts.Nash Equilibrium: no lock-in; meaning emerges whenever resolution permits
knockouts.Pragmatics: only calibration learning, nothing to lock

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: hedge informativeness is a smooth function of current resolution with no hysteresis

questions.distinguishing_observable: hysteresis: final MI differs between calibrate-then-talk and talk-while-calibrating schedules at the same final resolution

hypotheses.statement: Meaning as equilibrium-membership: an utterance's meaning is represented as the set of equilibria of the ongoing game it is consistent with; metacognitive confidence is the entropy over that set, so confidence is about which game is being played rather than about the world.

concept_contributions.Metacognition: entropy over candidate equilibria as confidence
concept_contributions.Nash Equilibrium: the equilibrium set as the hypothesis space

knockouts.Metacognition: no confidence; commit to first consistent equilibrium
knockouts.Pragmatics: no context narrowing; set stays large

questions.what_can_transfer: priors across games with isomorphic equilibrium structure
questions.distinguishing_observable: coordination success as a function of entropy-gated commitment vs immediate commitment

hypotheses.statement: Silence as an equilibrium speech act: agents may abstain from answering; whether silence means 'I do not know' or 'I will not say' is fixed by equilibrium and depends on whether abstention is driven by metacognitive uncertainty or by strategic withholding.

concept_contributions.Pragmatics: silence as meaningful by contrast with speaking

knockouts.Pragmatics: silence is a null action with no inference

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: abstention with a fixed penalty; listeners treat abstention as a coin flip

questions.what_exists: speakers with answer/abstain, listeners inferring from abstain
questions.what_can_transfer: the meaning of silence to a population with a different incentive
questions.distinguishing_observable: listener's posterior of speaker ignorance given silence vs actual rate

hypotheses.statement: Self-deceptive monitor: when outward confidence pays, a monitor whose internal calibration is shifted toward overconfidence is favoured over one that reports honestly-but-strategically, because the second pays a monitoring cost to maintain two confidence maps; inner and outer games are coupled through the cost of keeping private and public confidence distinct.

concept_contributions.Metacognition: internal confidence map and its cost

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: direct selection for overconfidence when it pays, with no two-map cost

questions.what_exists: agents with one or two confidence maps
questions.distinguishing_observable: internal ECE drift occurs only when two-map cost > 0

lenses.name: Hedge reliability diagram
lenses.rationale: Emergent tokens have no built-in meaning; the only way to read their meaning is the accuracy of answers they accompany.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: log of (token, correct) pairs at equilibrium
lenses.transformation: per-token accuracy and count; order tokens by accuracy
predictedSignals: tokens separate into distinct accuracy levels when metacognitive noise is low
lenses.nullExpectation: all tokens share the base accuracy; MI near 0
failureModes: tokens unused so accuracy estimates noisy
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: baseline public-meaning readout; other lenses are relative to it

lenses.name: Implicature ledger
lenses.rationale: Pragmatic meaning is visible exactly where listener action departs from what literal semantics would dictate.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: per-utterance record of literal-semantics action, actual listener action, context id
lenses.transformation: count departures from literal action; condition on context
observables: implicature success (departure led to correct referent)
predictedSignals: high implicature rate with high success in contexts with scalar alternatives
lenses.nullExpectation: departures at chance, success below literal baseline
failureModes: literal semantics ill-defined for emergent tokens

lenses.name: Deviation-regret audit
lenses.rationale: Claims about equilibrium require checking that no unilateral deviation pays, not that learning stopped.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: final strategy profile and the payoff simulator
lenses.transformation: for each role, evaluate every pure deviation by Monte Carlo; report max gain
observables: epsilon = max unilateral gain per role
predictedSignals: epsilon below tolerance at reported equilibria
lenses.nullExpectation: large epsilon if dynamics stalled away from equilibrium
failureModes: strategy space too large to enumerate
Monte Carlo noise mistaken for gain
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: certifies the Nash component, which the other lenses assume

lenses.name: Private-public calibration gap
lenses.rationale: The triplicate specifically predicts that what an agent knows about its accuracy and what its words say can diverge stably.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: per-item private confidence, public token, listener-decoded probability, correctness
lenses.transformation: compute ECE of private confidence, of token read at its original nominal value, and of listener-decoded probability
predictedSignals: gap > 0 while ECE_decoded stays small under confidence-weighting listeners
failureModes: nominal token values arbitrary, making ECE_public_literal a design choice

lenses.name: Recursion budget ledger
lenses.rationale: If metacognition controls pragmatic depth, depth spending should track item ambiguity.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: per-item depth used, item ambiguity (number of literal candidates), correctness
lenses.transformation: Spearman(depth, ambiguity); accuracy per depth step
predictedSignals: positive rank correlation; equal accuracy at lower mean depth than fixed depth
failureModes: ambiguity and depth both driven by context size
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: measures metacognitive efficiency of pragmatic computation, not outcome

lenses.name: Conflict-noise phase map
lenses.rationale: The three-way claim in M1 is an interaction: the interest conflict at which hedges collapse should depend on metacognitive noise.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: grid over (speaker bias b, metacognitive noise sigma) with equilibrium MI at each cell
lenses.transformation: for each sigma, locate b* where MI falls below half its b=0 value
failureModes: MI floor effects at high sigma make b* undefined
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: tests the interaction rather than the main effects, which the simpler alternative also predicts

experiments.hypothesis: The interest conflict at which emergent hedge tokens stop carrying information about correctness decreases as the speaker's metacognitive noise increases (interaction, not separable effects).
experiments.mechanism: Speaker answers a binary item correctly with prob q ~ U(0.5,1); observes private confidence c = q + N(0, sigma) clipped; maps c to one of K=3 tokens via 2 thresholds. Listener maps each token to accept/verify. Payoffs: listener +1 accept-correct, -2 accept-wrong, -0.3 verify; speaker gets listener payoff plus bias b per accept. Discrete strategy grids (thresholds on 0.05 grid) updated by smoothed best response in a population.
experiments.control: same world with sigma = infinity (confidence independent of q)
experiments.positive_control: speaker thresholds hard-coded to calibrated values and listener best-responding: MI must be >= 0.1 bits at sigma=0, b=0
experiments.observable: equilibrium MI(token; correct) per cell and b*(sigma) = smallest b with MI < 0.5 * MI(b=0)
experiments.success_criterion: median over 20 seeds: MI(sigma=0,b=0) >= 0.05 bits AND Spearman(b*, sigma) <= -0.8 across the 4 sigma levels AND b*(0) - b*(0.4) >= 0.25
experiments.failure_criterion: b* identical (difference < 0.25) across sigma levels, or MI(sigma=0,b=0) < 0.05 bits, or L3 epsilon > 0.02 at reported equilibria
experiments.alternative_explanation: noise lowers the stakes of accept decisions so any bias looks larger relative to them; the interaction is an artefact of the payoff scale, not of metacognitive access
experiments.null_twin: tokens conditioned on a confidence permuted across items within each seed (same marginal distribution of c, same token frequencies), destroying the c-q link while keeping sigma's effect on the confidence distribution
experiments.why_this_implementation: a finite strategy grid under best-response dynamics exposes equilibria directly and is auditable by L3; no learned function approximator needed
experiments.size: 50 speakers, 50 listeners, 3 tokens, 24 grid cells, 3000 rounds per cell, 20 seeds
stupid_explanations: MI estimator bias at small token counts produces apparent structure
best-response dynamics stalls in the initial random convention
payoff asymmetry (-2 vs +1) alone forces a two-level convention irrespective of confidence

experiments.hypothesis: The listener's clarification threshold and the speaker's redundancy form an interior equilibrium whose threshold falls as clarification cost rises, and this depends on the listener using its own posterior as the trigger.
experiments.mechanism: 8 objects with 3 binary features per trial; speaker names r in {1,2,3} features of the target at cost 0.05 per word; listener computes posterior over consistent objects, clarifies if max posterior < tau at cost k (then succeeds), else guesses. Payoff shared: +1 success minus costs. Strategy grid tau in {0,0.1,...,1}, r in {1,2,3}; equilibrium by iterated best response on a Monte Carlo payoff table.
experiments.control: listener clarifies at a fixed tau = 0.5 regardless of k
experiments.positive_control: k = 0: equilibrium must be tau = 1 or r = 3 with success >= 0.99
experiments.observable: tau*(k), r*(k), success rate at equilibrium
experiments.success_criterion: median over 20 seeds: Spearman(tau*, k) <= -0.8 AND equilibrium success minus null-twin success >= 0.10 at k = 0.1
experiments.failure_criterion: tau* constant across k, or null twin success within 0.05 of the mechanism
experiments.alternative_explanation: the effect is the ARQ trade-off of any noisy channel; pragmatics adds nothing
experiments.null_twin: listener's clarification trigger uses a random score drawn from the empirical marginal of its posterior-max (same clarification rate distribution, no link to actual ambiguity)
experiments.why_this_implementation: exact enumeration of consistent objects makes the listener's posterior exact, so metacognitive access is controlled precisely
experiments.size: 8 objects, 3 features, 11 x 3 strategy grid, 5000 trials per cell, 6 cost levels, 20 seeds
stupid_explanations: random feature sets often make the target unique, so clarification barely matters
the tau grid is too coarse for an interior optimum to move
shared payoff makes it a team decision problem where 'equilibrium' is just an optimum

experiments.hypothesis: A listener that stops recursive pragmatic reasoning when its interpretive uncertainty is low reaches the accuracy of fixed-depth reasoning with fewer recursion steps, and its depth tracks item ambiguity.
experiments.mechanism: Symbolic referential contexts of 3-4 objects over a scalar lexicon (e.g. 'some'/'all' style predicates); literal listener L0, speaker S1, listener L1, up to L3 computed exactly by normalized tables; adaptive listener stops at level k when max posterior >= theta. Speakers are fixed S2 in this minimal world.
experiments.positive_control: items with a unique literal referent must be solved at depth 0 by the adaptive listener
experiments.observable: accuracy, mean depth, Spearman(depth, number of literal candidates)
experiments.success_criterion: for some theta: accuracy >= accuracy(L2) - 0.01 AND mean depth <= 0.7 * 2 AND Spearman(depth, ambiguity) >= 0.4
experiments.failure_criterion: no theta meets all three, or the random-depth twin with matched mean depth meets the accuracy criterion too
experiments.alternative_explanation: most items are unambiguous so any early stopping saves depth; the result reflects the item distribution, not metacognition
experiments.null_twin: depth drawn at random per item from the adaptive listener's empirical depth distribution (same mean and variance), ignoring uncertainty
experiments.why_this_implementation: exact probabilistic tables over tiny contexts avoid learned approximators; recursion depth is literal and countable
experiments.size: 2000 random contexts of 3-4 objects, 4 predicates, depth up to 3, 10 seeds
stupid_explanations: ambiguity is correlated with context size, so depth tracks size not uncertainty
deeper levels rarely change the answer, so any stopping rule is as good
the S2 speaker makes the task trivially solvable at L1

experiments.hypothesis: When listeners reward stated confidence, a stable convention forms in which public confidence words are shifted from private calibrated confidence while listener-decoded confidence remains calibrated; under proper-scoring listeners the shift vanishes.
experiments.mechanism: Speakers have calibrated private confidence c on binary items and choose a word from 5 ordered words with nominal values {0.55,0.65,0.75,0.85,0.95}. Listener regime A pays speakers proportional to decoded confidence of accepted answers; regime B pays by Brier score of decoded confidence. Listeners learn a decoding table word -> probability from outcomes. Replicator dynamics over speaker word maps (monotone maps on a grid).
experiments.positive_control: speakers forced to use the nominal honest map: gap must be <= 0.02 in both regimes
experiments.success_criterion: median over 20 seeds: gap_A >= 0.08 AND gap_B <= 0.03 AND ECE_decoded_A <= 0.05
experiments.failure_criterion: gap_A < 0.05, or ECE_decoded_A > 0.10 (no stable discounting convention), or L3 epsilon > 0.02
experiments.alternative_explanation: regime A simply rewards the top word, so speakers pile onto it; the 'convention' is saturation plus a one-token decoder
experiments.null_twin: regime A with listeners' decoding table frozen at nominal values (no pragmatic discounting), keeping the same payoff scale
experiments.why_this_implementation: replicator dynamics over a small monotone-map space gives equilibria that can be audited exhaustively
experiments.size: 100 speakers, 100 listeners, 5 words, 5000 rounds, 2 regimes, 20 seeds
stupid_explanations: saturation on the top word makes ECE_public_literal large by construction
ECE binning artefacts with only 5 words
the decoded ECE is low merely because one word carries almost all mass
